_comment: The axe rules this harness is allowed to plant, and which humane skill may
own each finding. An ALLOW-LIST, never a deny-list: the enabled rule set is
the oracle, so an axe-core upgrade that adds a layout-dependent rule must
not silently join it. axe-core is pinned exactly in package.json for the
A rule is here only if CLAUDE.md's ownership table gives it an owner.
'Accessibility engineering depth' is explicitly OUT of humane's scope and
deferred to interfaces/better-accessibility, so the accessible-name rules
(image-alt, label, button-name, link-name) are excluded: planting a defect
the method disclaims would test nothing about the method, and would punish a
review for correctly routing it elsewhere.
accepted_owners is a SET, not one name. Some defects are defensibly routed
to more than one skill, and routing_accuracy must not mark a defensible

heading-order.why: Heading hierarchy is structure. layout-rules owns structural and interaction defect classes.

region.why: Content outside any landmark is a structural omission.

landmark-one-main.why: A missing main landmark is a structural omission.

page-has-heading-one.why: Document hierarchy has no top. Structure, not wording.

empty-heading.why: A heading with no text is both a missing string (ux-writing owns what a string says) and a hierarchy break. Either routing is defensible.

html-has-lang.why: layout-rules owns the i18n/theming rule group.

excluded.color-contrast: Owned by oracle #1 (dtokens/contrast.py), which measures APCA and WCAG under standard=both. axe is WCAG-only and would contradict the deliberately planted WCAG-pass/APCA-fail pairs. Under jsdom axe cannot decide it at all — it returns `incomplete`, not a verdict.
